common_name: knee chest lumbar lower back stretch
why: Gently decompresses lumbar vertebrae and releases erector spinae to relieve general lower back aching.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Lie):** Lie on back, knees bent. **STEP 2 (Hug):** Draw both knees simultaneously toward chest and wrap arms around shins. **STEP 3 (Rock):** Gently rock side to side 30 seconds, then hold still 30 seconds.

common_name: quadratus lumborum left lower back stretch QL
why: Directly lengthens the left quadratus lumborum — the muscle responsible for lateral lower back pain and hip-hike.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Stand):** Stand feet hip-width. **STEP 2 (Side bend):** Reach right arm overhead and lean to RIGHT — you stretch the LEFT side. **STEP 3 (Anchor):** Place left hand on left hip for support. Hold 30 seconds.

common_name: quadratus lumborum right lower back QL
why: Lengthens the right quadratus lumborum to relieve right-sided lower back pain and lumbar tightness.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Stand):** Stand feet hip-width. **STEP 2 (Side bend):** Reach left arm overhead and lean to LEFT — stretches the RIGHT side. **STEP 3 (Anchor):** Place right hand on right hip. Hold 30 seconds.

common_name: coccyx tailbone relief forward lean supine tilt
why: Tilts pelvis forward to unload pressure from the coccyx — immediate relief for tailbone (coccydynia) pain after sitting.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Sit):** Sit on edge of firm chair. **STEP 2 (Lean):** Lean weight slightly forward onto thighs, tilting pelvis forward. This lifts coccyx off seat. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Maintain tilt for 30 seconds, breathing normally.
process: Do this on standing up after sitting. 5 reps x 30 seconds.

common_name: sacral rocking sacrum coccyx tailbone lumbar
why: Provides gentle rhythmic mobilisation of the sacrum and coccyx — reduces compressive coccydynia pain through joint oscillation.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Lie):** Lie on back, knees bent, feet flat. **STEP 2 (Tilt):** Flatten low back into floor (posterior tilt), hold 3 seconds. **STEP 3 (Arch):** Arch low back up (anterior tilt), hold 3 seconds. Rock between the two.
process: 15-20 slow cycles. Focus on moving tailbone away from floor, then toward it.

common_name: sacroiliac joint sacrum release lower back lumbar
why: Gently gaps the sacroiliac joint to relieve deep unilateral sacral pain characteristic of SI joint dysfunction.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Lie):** Lie on back, knees bent. **STEP 2 (Drop):** Let both knees drop slowly to right, feeling gentle rotation through sacrum. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Hold 45 seconds, then return centre and drop left.

common_name: double knee chest sacrum coccyx lumbar lumborum
why: Flexing both hips simultaneously flattens and releases the sacrum against floor, relieving sacral compression.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Lie):** Lie flat. Hug both knees to chest at same time, sacrum pressing into floor. **STEP 2 (Hold):** Hold the hug firmly for 45 seconds. **STEP 3 (Rock):** Gently rock left and right 10 times before releasing.

common_name: cat cow lumbar lower back erector
why: Rhythmically flexes and extends the lumbar spine to reduce stiffness in L1-L5 joints and warm up paraspinals.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Tabletop):** On hands and knees, wrists under shoulders. **STEP 2 (Cat):** Exhale and round lower back toward ceiling. **STEP 3 (Cow):** Inhale and let lower back arch, pelvis tilting forward.

common_name: press up extension lumbar erector lower back McKenzie
why: McKenzie-style lumbar extension that centralises disc-related pain and opens the anterior disc space to relieve nerve compression.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Prone):** Lie face down, hands under shoulders. **STEP 2 (Press):** Slowly straighten elbows, letting pelvis stay on floor as back arches. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Hold at top 10 seconds, lower with control.
process: 10 reps, 2-3 sets. Stop if pain increases.

common_name: childs pose lumbar lower back stretch yoga
why: Passively decompresses every lumbar vertebra and provides full spine-length traction using body weight.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Kneel):** Kneel and sit back toward heels. **STEP 2 (Extend):** Reach arms forward on floor. **STEP 3 (Sink):** Let chest drop toward thighs and breathe deeply into lower back. Hold 2 minutes.
process: 2-3 minutes. Use as go-to rest position throughout the day.

common_name: supine twist lower back lumbar yoga rotation
why: Rotates and decompresses lumbar facet joints, releasing torsional stiffness that aches after sitting.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Lie):** Lie on back. Bring right knee to chest. **STEP 2 (Cross):** Guide right knee across body to left using left hand. **STEP 3 (Open):** Extend right arm to right and look right. Hold 1 minute each side.

common_name: bird dog erector lower back lumbar spinae core
why: Trains erector spinae, multifidus, and glutes in coordinated stability — the foundation of lasting lower back health.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Tabletop):** On hands and knees. **STEP 2 (Extend):** Simultaneously extend right arm and left leg until both horizontal. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Hold 5 seconds, then switch sides. Focus on not rotating hips.

common_name: pelvic tilt lower back lumbar erector posture
why: Teaches the pelvis to find neutral — the most important posture habit for preventing recurring lower back pain.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Lie):** Lie on back, knees bent. **STEP 2 (Flatten):** Gently tighten lower abdomen and press back flat to floor. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Hold 10 seconds, breathe normally, release.
process: 15 reps x 2 sets. Also practise standing against a wall.

common_name: hip circle lower back warmup lumbar
why: Warms the lumbar joints, hip flexors, and QL through their full rotary range before physical activity.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Stand):** Feet slightly wider than shoulder-width, hands on hips. **STEP 2 (Circle):** Make large slow circles with hips — 10 clockwise. **STEP 3 (Reverse):** 10 counter-clockwise.
process: 10 circles each direction. Gradually increase size.

common_name: belly breathing diaphragm abdominal release
why: Deep belly breathing reduces intra-abdominal pressure, releases the diaphragm, and deactivates abdominal guarding.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Lie):** Lie on back, one hand on stomach. **STEP 2 (Inhale):** Breathe in slowly through nose for 4 counts — let belly rise, not chest. **STEP 3 (Exhale):** Exhale slowly for 6 counts, letting belly fall.
process: 10 deep cycles. Use as an ongoing reset whenever discomfort spikes.

common_name: upper abdominal massage rectus stomach
why: Gentle circular massage over the epigastric region releases muscle tightness and improves visceral motility.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Lie):** Lie on back, knees bent. **STEP 2 (Press):** Using three fingertips, apply gentle clockwise circular pressure below ribcage. **STEP 3 (Move):** Work slowly across upper abdomen from right to left.

common_name: lower abdominal release rectus oblique
why: Reduces tension in the lower rectus abdominis and hip flexor attachment causing low abdominal cramping.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Prone):** Lie face down with pillow under lower abdomen. **STEP 2 (Breathe):** Take 10 slow deep breaths letting gravity gently decompress lower belly. **STEP 3 (Relax):** Focus on fully relaxing abdomen with each exhale.

common_name: dead bug abdominal core transverse rectus
why: Trains deep transverse abdominis against limb loading — a safe spine-neutral core exercise for all levels.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Lie):** Lie on back, arms and knees pointing to ceiling at 90 degrees. **STEP 2 (Brace):** Press low back to floor. **STEP 3 (Extend):** Simultaneously lower right arm overhead and left leg toward floor. Return, switch.
process: 8 reps per side, 3 sets. Never let back lift.

common_name: plank core abdominal rectus oblique stabiliser
why: Builds endurance in rectus abdominis and obliques in their supporting role — safer for spine than crunches.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Forearm):** Forearms on floor, elbows under shoulders. Body in one straight line. **STEP 2 (Squeeze):** Brace core, squeeze glutes, keep hips level. **STEP 3 (Breathe):** Breathe slowly and hold.
process: Start at 20 seconds, build to 60 seconds. 3 sets.

common_name: pallof press oblique left side core
why: Anti-rotation training for the left obliques — prevents side-flexion weakness leading to lateral abdominal strain.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Band):** Anchor band to your right. Stand sideways. **STEP 2 (Press):** Hold band at chest and press it straight forward. **STEP 3 (Resist):** Resist the pull from rotating — hold 3 seconds per rep.

common_name: TVA transverse abdominis activation core posture
why: Rehabilitates the deep transverse abdominis — the inner corset whose weakness causes abdominal wall pain and recurrence.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Hook):** Lie on back, knees bent. **STEP 2 (Draw):** Gently draw belly button toward floor without moving pelvis or ribs. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Hold 10 seconds, breathe out naturally. Release and repeat.
process: 15 reps x 2 sets, twice per day.

common_name: boat pose core abdominal yoga modification
why: Activates hip flexors and rectus abdominis in neutral spinal position to re-awaken abdominal tone.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Sit):** Sit with knees bent, feet flat. **STEP 2 (Lean):** Lean back slightly until abdominal tension felt. **STEP 3 (Lift):** Option: lift feet off ground to deepen.

common_name: hip flexor lunge stretch iliopsoas
why: Directly lengthens the iliopsoas — relieves the pulling ache at the front of the hip after prolonged sitting.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Kneel):** Kneel on right knee, left foot forward. **STEP 2 (Sink):** Push hips forward and down until stretch deep in front of right hip. **STEP 3 (Raise):** Raise right arm overhead to increase iliopsoas stretch. Hold 45 seconds.

common_name: groin adductor stretch hip inner thigh
why: Stretches adductor longus at the groin crease — relieves sharp pulling pain in inner hip from kicking or prolonged striding.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Squat):** Sit in wide squat, feet wide, toes out. **STEP 2 (Elbows):** Place elbows on inner thighs. **STEP 3 (Press):** Gently press elbows outward to deepen inner groin stretch. Hold 45 seconds.

common_name: figure four hip stretch piriformis left
why: Stretches left gluteus medius and external hip rotators to relieve lateral hip socket pain.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Lie):** Lie on back, knees bent. **STEP 2 (Cross):** Cross left ankle over right knee. **STEP 3 (Pull):** Reach through and pull right thigh toward chest. Hold 45 seconds.

common_name: figure four hip stretch piriformis right
why: Stretches right gluteus medius and hip external rotators to relieve right hip socket pain.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Lie):** Lie on back, knees bent. **STEP 2 (Cross):** Cross right ankle over left knee. **STEP 3 (Pull):** Pull left thigh toward chest. Hold 45 seconds.

common_name: iliopsoas thomas stretch hip flexor
why: Isolates the iliopsoas by locking the pelvis, providing a deeper and more targeted hip flexor release than a standing lunge.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Edge):** Sit on edge of table. **STEP 2 (Lie):** Lie back and bring both knees to chest. **STEP 3 (Lower):** Let right leg drop over edge. Feel stretch in right hip flexor. Hold 45 seconds.

common_name: hip circle warmup iliopsoas tensor
why: Lubricates the hip socket through full circumduction to raise temperature and synovial fluid before lower-body exercise.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Stand):** Stand on one leg. **STEP 2 (Circle):** Make large circle with opposite knee — 10 forward. **STEP 3 (Reverse):** 10 backward. Switch legs.

common_name: pigeon pose hip yoga iliopsoas
why: The most effective single pose for releasing the entire hip complex — opens hip flexors, rotators, and joint capsule.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Dog):** Start in downward dog. **STEP 2 (Swing):** Bring right knee forward to right wrist, shin angled across. **STEP 3 (Lower):** Lower hips toward floor. Hold 2 minutes.

common_name: clamshell hip abductor tensor Exercise
why: Isolates gluteus medius — the primary hip stabiliser that when weak causes hip labrum overload and lateral pain.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Side):** Lie on side, hips and knees bent 45 degrees, band above knees. **STEP 2 (Open):** Keeping feet together, lift top knee like a clamshell opening. **STEP 3 (Control):** Lower slowly without letting pelvis rock.

common_name: posterior pelvic tilt hip posture iliopsoas
why: Teaches pelvis to rest in neutral against wall, correcting anterior pelvic tilt that shortens hip flexors.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Wall):** Stand with back against wall, feet 5cm away. **STEP 2 (Flatten):** Gently tighten glutes and press lower back flat to wall. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Hold 10 seconds, release, repeat.

common_name: figure four gluteus glute stretch left
why: Deep stretch of the left gluteus maximus and external hip rotators — relieves the dull spreading ache of the left buttock.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Lie):** Back on floor, knees bent. **STEP 2 (Cross):** Cross left ankle over right knee. **STEP 3 (Pull):** Pull right thigh to chest. Hold 45 seconds.

common_name: figure four gluteus glute stretch right
why: Deeply stretches the right gluteus maximus and hip external rotators.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Lie):** Back on floor, knees bent. **STEP 2 (Cross):** Cross right ankle over left knee. **STEP 3 (Pull):** Pull left thigh to chest. Hold 45 seconds.

common_name: piriformis stretch deep glute sciatic
why: Targets the deep piriformis which when tight compresses the sciatic nerve causing deep glute and leg pain.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Sit):** Sit in chair. Cross right ankle over left knee. **STEP 2 (Hinge):** Gently hinge forward from hips, keeping back straight. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Hold when you feel deep ache in right buttock. Hold 45 seconds.

common_name: supine coccyx tilt tailbone coccydynia glute
why: Gently mobilises the coccyx through posterior tilt, decompressing the inflamed coccygeal joint — primary source of tailbone pain.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Lie):** Lie on back, knees bent, feet flat. **STEP 2 (Tilt):** Gently tilt pelvis backward — tailbone presses lightly into floor, then lifts. **STEP 3 (Rock):** Slowly rock tailbone down and up, 15 gentle repetitions.
process: 15-20 gentle rocks, 2-3 times daily. Stop if sharp pain occurs.

common_name: happy baby pose glute coccyx tailbone
why: Opens sacro-iliac joints and lifts coccyx free of compressive forces — excellent after long periods of sitting.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Lie):** Lie on back. Draw knees toward chest. **STEP 2 (Grab):** Reach inside legs and hold outer edges of feet (or shins). **STEP 3 (Open):** Gently pull knees toward floor beside torso. Hold 1-2 minutes.
process: 1-2 minutes. Rock gently side to side to massage sacrum.

common_name: prone piriformis stretch deep glute sciatic
why: The prone position fully internally rotates the hip, providing a more complete piriformis stretch than seated version.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Prone):** Lie face down. **STEP 2 (Bend):** Bend right knee to 90 degrees and drop it outward so shin is across back. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Place folded blanket under right hip for support. Hold 1 minute.

common_name: glute bridge warmup gluteus maximus
why: Activates glutes and warms hip extensors through full range — primes the posterior chain before exercise.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Lie):** On back, knees bent, feet flat. **STEP 2 (Press):** Press through heels and lift hips until they form straight line with knees. **STEP 3 (Squeeze):** Squeeze glutes at top 1 second. Lower slowly.

common_name: pigeon pose glute yoga gluteus
why: Long-held pigeon pose releases deep fascia of glutes and external rotators for lasting softening.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Dog):** Downward dog. **STEP 2 (Bring):** Bring right knee to right wrist, shin angled. **STEP 3 (Sink):** Lower hips to floor and fold forward over front shin. Hold 3 minutes.
process: 3 minutes per side — this is a yin (passive) hold.

common_name: glute bridge strength gluteus maximus
why: Rebuilds gluteus maximus strength — when weak it causes chronic low back, SI joint, and tailbone loading.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Lie):** Back on floor, knees bent. **STEP 2 (Drive):** Press heels into floor, drive hips to ceiling, squeezing glutes. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Hold 2 seconds at top. Lower with control.

common_name: single leg glute bridge gluteus hip thrust
why: Progresses glute strength unilaterally — identifies and corrects side-to-side imbalance driving asymmetric buttock pain.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Lie):** Back on floor, one knee bent, one leg straight. **STEP 2 (Drive):** Drive through planted heel and lift hips high. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Keep straight leg elevated throughout. Hold 2 seconds at top.

common_name: quadriceps standing quad stretch front thigh femor
why: Lengthens rectus femoris from hip to knee — relieves anterior thigh tightness and referred knee pain from quad overuse.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Stand):** Stand on left leg, holding wall for balance. **STEP 2 (Bend):** Bend right knee and hold ankle behind you. **STEP 3 (Tuck):** Gently tuck pelvis (tighten glutes) to increase stretch. Hold 30 seconds.

common_name: hamstring stretch back thigh seated
why: Lengthens hamstrings from ischial tuberosity to knee, relieving posterior thigh aching caused by sitting.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Sit):** Sit on edge of chair, one leg extended heel on floor. **STEP 2 (Hinge):** Hinge forward from hips — keep back straight, not rounded. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Feel pull along back of extended thigh. Hold 30 seconds.

common_name: adductor inner thigh stretch groin femor
why: Lengthens all five adductors along inner thigh — relieves groin-referred inner thigh pain from hip tightness.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Wide):** Stand with feet wide, toes out 45 degrees. **STEP 2 (Shift):** Shift weight to right, bending right knee, keeping left leg straight. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Feel pull along left inner thigh. Hold 30 seconds per side.

common_name: IT band tensor outer thigh stretch
why: Stretches the iliotibial band and outer quad to relieve the tight burning sensation along the outer thigh.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Cross):** Stand and cross right leg behind left. **STEP 2 (Lean):** Lean to left, pushing right hip outward. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Feel pull along outer right thigh. Hold 30 seconds.

common_name: supine hamstring stretch back thigh femor
why: Lying hamstring stretch that relaxes the entire posterior chain — more effective than standing for tight or painful thighs.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Lie):** Lie on back. **STEP 2 (Lift):** Raise right leg and hold behind thigh or calf. **STEP 3 (Straighten):** Gently straighten knee as far as comfortable. Hold 30 seconds.

common_name: leg swing hamstring quadriceps thigh warmup
why: Dynamically moves the hip through flexion/extension arc to warm quadriceps and hamstrings before running.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Hold):** Stand next to wall for support. **STEP 2 (Swing):** Swing outer leg forward and back like a pendulum — loose and relaxed. **STEP 3 (Increase):** Gradually increase arc over 10 swings.
process: 15 swings per leg, 2 planes (front-back and across body).

common_name: warrior one quadriceps front thigh yoga
why: Deeply opens the hip flexor and rectus femoris of the back leg in a grounded stable stance.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Step):** Step right foot forward, left foot back at 45 degrees. **STEP 2 (Sink):** Bend right knee to 90 degrees. **STEP 3 (Lift):** Raise arms overhead. Tuck pelvis under to increase quad stretch. Hold 45 seconds.

common_name: seated forward fold hamstring back thigh yoga
why: Yin-style passive stretch of entire hamstring chain — excellent for chronic back-thigh tightness.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Sit):** Straight-leg sit on floor. **STEP 2 (Hinge):** Hinge forward from hips with flat back as far as comfortable. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Rest hands on shins, calves, or feet. Hold 2 minutes.
process: 2 minutes. Breathe into back of thighs.

common_name: frog pose adductor inner thigh yoga
why: The most complete inner thigh stretch — opens both hip joints simultaneously with deep adductor lengthening.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Tabletop):** From hands and knees. **STEP 2 (Widen):** Slowly walk knees wide apart, feet flexed beside each knee. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Lower to forearms, hold 2 minutes.
process: 2 minutes. Use folded blanket under each knee if needed.

common_name: bodyweight squat quadriceps thigh femor
why: Rebuilds quad, hamstring, and glute strength — the most functional exercise for thigh health and pain prevention.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Feet):** Stand feet shoulder-width, toes out 15 degrees. **STEP 2 (Sink):** Hinge hips back and bend knees — lower until thighs parallel floor. **STEP 3 (Rise):** Drive through heels to stand. Squeeze glutes at top.

common_name: hip flexor reset quad front thigh posture
why: Recalibrates the resting length of hip flexors — when short they tilt pelvis forward, creating chronic anterior thigh tightness.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Lie):** Lie on back. **STEP 2 (Hug):** Draw one knee to chest and hold it. **STEP 3 (Extend):** Let the other leg rest flat on floor. If the flat leg's heel lifts, hip flexor is short.
process: 2 minutes per side daily. Focus on letting straight leg relax fully.

common_name: hamstring curl thigh back femor resistance
why: Directly strengthens the hamstrings to correct weakness that leads to posterior thigh strains.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Lie):** Lie face down, band looped around ankle anchored beneath door. **STEP 2 (Curl):** Bend knee, curling heel toward glutes. **STEP 3 (Lower):** Lower slowly against band resistance.
